According to the document, delamination typically takes a couple hours to be completed at room temperature, while less than 2 min are needed when increasing the reaction temperature to 100 °C. At 160 °C, delamination takes about 6 s. At the boiling point of ethylene glycol (198 °C), delamination takes about 2 s.

To calculate how many times faster delamination is at the boiling point of ethylene glycol than at 160 °C, we can divide the time it takes at 160 °C (6 s) by the time it takes at the boiling point (2 s):

6 s / 2 s = 3

So, delamination is 3 times faster at the boiling point of ethylene glycol than at 160 °C.

The boiling point of ethylene glycol is 198 °C.
